name: Cordillera Blanca & Huaraz
why: The four-day Santa Cruz trek crosses Punta Unión near 4,750 m, and the Laguna 69 day hike is the area's signature. The tropics' highest mountain range, and a different trip from Cusco. Best: May–Sep. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list (same name) in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: One range and its base town, one trip.

name: Julian Alps & Primorska
why: Triglav National Park around Mount Triglav, Lake Bohinj and the Soča Valley, with the roughly 330 km, 20-stage Juliana Trail loop for long walks. Compact, hut-supported alpine hiking at a fraction of the Dolomites' crowds. Best: Late Jun–Sep (Jul–Aug busiest; June and September quieter). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: A small country's alpine heart, one trip.

name: Himachal & Garhwal Himalaya
why: The Valley of Flowers, Har Ki Dun, Triund, the Hampta Pass and the high desert of Spiti: the lower Indian Himalaya's answer to Nepal, with village-to-village and camping routes. Best: Late Jun–Sep (Valley of Flowers bloom in Jul–Aug; the monsoon needs care). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: Two Indian states, but one Himalayan hiking region.

name: Drakensberg
why: The Amphitheatre walk to the top of Tugela Falls (about 12 km, 5–6 hours, with chain ladders), Cathedral Peak and Giant's Castle. South Africa's mountain hiking, and a different world from the Cape coast. Best: Apr–May (autumn); spring second-best. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: One escarpment range, one trip.

name: Corsica
why: The GR20 is a hut-to-hut route of roughly 180 km, widely called Europe's toughest long trail, with gentler Mare a Mare crossings and coastal paths like the Calanches de Piana. Sardinia is its nearest sibling. Best: GR20 late Jun–early Sep; lower routes Apr–Oct. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: An island, one decision.

name: Grand Teton & Jackson Hole
why: Cascade Canyon, Paintbrush Divide and the overnight Teton Crest Trail rise straight from the valley floor. Usually paired with Yellowstone but a separate park with far better day hikes. Best: Jul–Sep. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list (same name) in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: One national park and its town, one trip.

name: Aoraki / Mount Cook
why: New Zealand's highest mountain, with the Hooker Valley Track, the Tasman Glacier lake and the steep Mueller Hut route. A 3-hour drive from Queenstown, so a separate stop rather than a day trip. Best: Dec–Apr. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list (same name) in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: One national park and its village, one trip.

name: Kauai
why: The Kalalau Trail along the Nāpali Coast (11 miles one way, camping permit beyond Hanakāpīʻai, day-use reservations at Haʻena), plus Waimea Canyon and the Kōkeʻe plateau trails. The Hawaiian island with the most dramatic hiking, and not in the catalog. Best: Apr–Oct is the more reliable season; the north shore is wet in winter. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the surfing list (same name).
grainNote: An island, one decision.

name: Aragonese Pyrenees
why: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park, with its canyon walls and waterfall trails, plus the Posets–Maladeta peaks and the Gavarnie cirque just over the French border. The Pyrenees' best-known day hikes and hut routes. Best: Jun–Sep. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: The central Pyrenees, one trip.

name: Tyrol
why: Hut-to-hut classics like the Stubai High Trail, the Zillertal and Ötztal ranges, and Hohe Tauern National Park around the Grossglockner. Austria is the Alps' deepest hut network and has no place in the catalog beyond Vienna. Best: Jul–Sep (huts open roughly late June to late September). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: One Alpine state, hut-to-hut country.

name: Picos de Europa
why: Limestone peaks a few miles from the Atlantic, with the Cares Gorge path, the Covadonga lakes and the Naranjo de Bulnes pinnacle. Spain's first national park, with easy, dramatic day hikes plus high routes. Best: Jun–Sep for the high routes; May and October for the gorges. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list (as "Picos de Europa") in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: One national park massif, one trip.

name: Japanese Northern Alps
why: Kamikochi, Hakuba and the Tateyama–Kurobe route offer the best mountain hiking in Japan, with hut-to-hut ridges and a strong transport network. Tokyo & Kyoto covers city and temple walking only. Best: Jul–mid Oct (Kamikochi is open roughly mid-April to mid-November). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: One mountain range, one trip.

name: Tatra Mountains
why: The High Tatras are the highest range of the Carpathians, with Zakopane and Morskie Oko on the Polish side and Štrbské Pleso on the Slovak side, and a ridge-and-lake hiking network with mountain huts. Rysy is the classic summit day. Best: Jun–Sep (higher routes snowbound until about late June). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: One range across a border, one decision.

name: Albanian Alps & Montenegro
why: The Theth-to-Valbona crossing (about 14–17 km, 7–9 hours, over a pass near 1,800 m) is the signature day, with the longer Peaks of the Balkans route linking Albania, Kosovo and Montenegro, and Durmitor nearby. Guesthouse-to-guesthouse hiking with few crowds. Best: Jun–Sep (snow on the passes until late May, sometimes July). (Real, specialist-known. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: One mountain range (the Accursed Mountains), one trip.

name: Mount Rainier
why: The 93-mile Wonderland Trail circles the volcano; the Skyline Trail and Paradise meadows are the classic day hikes. Close to Seattle, and a different park from North Cascades. Best: Jul–Sep (wildflowers peak late Jul–Aug). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list in the old Catalog Wishlist (as "Mount Rainier & the Cascades"; not yet imported).
grainNote: One national park, one trip.

name: White Mountains
why: The Presidential Range, Franconia Ridge and Mount Washington (known for severe weather) are served by the Appalachian Mountain Club's hut system. The East's biggest above-treeline hiking. Best: Jun–Oct (fall color late Sep–early Oct). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: One range, one trip.

name: Newfoundland
why: Gros Morne's tablelands and fjord country, with Gros Morne Mountain and the Long Range Traverse, and the 336 km East Coast Trail along cliffs and sea-stack coves near St. John's. Icebergs and whales in the early summer. Best: Jul–Sep. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: An island, but Gros Morne and St. John's are 650 km apart.

name: Réunion Island
why: The volcanic cirques of Mafate (no roads), Cilaos and Salazie, the GR R1 loop and the Piton des Neiges. A French territory with some of the Indian Ocean's best hiking, and a different island from Mauritius. Best: May–Nov (the dry season). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the whale-watching list (same name).
grainNote: An island, one decision.

name: Crete
why: The Samaria Gorge (about 16 km), the E4 coastal path and the Lefka Ori (White Mountains) give Crete the best hiking in Greece outside the mainland. The Cyclades text covers Santorini only. Best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct (the Samaria Gorge is open roughly May–Oct). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: An island, one decision.

name: Carretera Austral
why: Cerro Castillo's four-day circuit, the Queulat hanging glacier and Pumalín Park. Wild, uncrowded northern Patagonia, well north of Torres del Paine and El Chaltén. Best: Dec–Mar. (Real, specialist-known. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: A 1,200 km road region, but the hiking stops cluster in Aysén.

name: Dominica
why: The Waitukubuli National Trail crosses the island in 14 segments, with the Boiling Lake hike through Morne Trois Pitons National Park. The Caribbean's best rainforest hiking and a short flight from Barbados. Best: Dec–May (the dry season). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the diving list (same name) and the whale-watching list (same name).
grainNote: An island country, one decision. Not the Dominican Republic.

name: Swedish Lapland & Kungsleden
why: The Kungsleden ("King's Trail") runs about 440 km through arctic Sweden, with the classic Abisko–Nikkaluokta section past Kebnekaise, plus the wild Sarek park. Huts and a marked path make it the Nordic region's easiest big trek. Best: Late Jun–early Sep (August has fewer mosquitoes). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: One trail region, one trip.

name: Yunnan
why: The Tiger Leaping Gorge high road (a two-day hike above the Yangtze), the Meili Snow Mountain and Yubeng valleys, and the Lijiang plateau. China's best-known trekking outside Tibet. Best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov (summer is the wet season). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the birding list (same name).
grainNote: A province, but Lijiang to Shangri-La is one trip.

name: Galicia
region: Northwest Spain; the Camino de Santiago
why: The final stretch of the Camino de Santiago runs through Galicia (the last 100 km from Sarria is the usual minimum walk), alongside the Atlantic Rías coast and the Cíes Islands. Chosen as "Galicia" rather than the whole 780 km Camino Francés, which is a route rather than a place. Best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct. (Established. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: A region, with the Camino as its anchor.

name: Cordillera Real
why: The Choro Trail descends about three days from the Andean divide to the Yungas jungle, with Huayna Potosí and the lake-and-peak trails above La Paz. Bolivia's trekking, and cheaper and quieter than Peru. Best: May–Sep. (Real, specialist-known. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the mountaineering list (same name) in the old Catalog Wishlist (not yet imported).
grainNote: One range, one base city.

name: Cape Verde Islands
why: Santo Antão's Cova–Paúl–Ponta do Sol descent is the signature hike, with Fogo's volcano as a second draw. Atlantic island hiking in the same spirit as the Canaries. Best: Nov–Jun (the dry season). (Established. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the birding list (Cape Verde Shearwater, Raso Lark) and the diving list (same name).
grainNote: An island country chosen first; the island comes later.

name: Copper Canyon
why: The Barrancas del Cobre, a network of canyons often described as larger than the Grand Canyon, with village-to-village trails to Urique and Batopilas and the Rarámuri (Tarahumara) people. A long-distance rail-and-trek trip. Best: Oct–Nov and Mar–Apr (the canyon floor is very hot in summer). (Real, specialist-known. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: One canyon system, one trip.

name: Oman
why: The Jebel Akhdar plateau and its Balcony Walk, the Jebel Shams canyon rim above Wadi Ghul, and wadi hikes such as Wadi Shab. Cool-season canyon hiking next to Jordan in spirit. Best: Oct–Apr. (Real, specialist-known. Researched Oct 2026.) ↳ Also on the wildlife-viewing list (same name; Arabian oryx and turtles — a different part of the country).
grainNote: A country, but its hiking sits in one mountain range.

name: Chapada Diamantina
why: Tabletop mountains, waterfalls and caves, with the multi-day Vale do Pati trek and the Fumaça waterfall viewpoint. Brazil's best hiking outside the Atlantic mountains. Best: May–Sep. (Real, specialist-known. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: One national park, one trip.

name: Romanian Carpathians
why: The Făgăraș ridge (home of Romania's highest peaks), Piatra Craiului and Retezat offer wild ridge hiking with huts and bears in the forests below. Little-visited compared with the Alps. Best: Jul–Sep. (Real, specialist-known. Researched Oct 2026.)
grainNote: A long range, but Transylvania works as one trip.
